- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00–0.20), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at +5–10% above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 85+), model overreacts; reduce forecast momentum and align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- When sentiment is positive (0.20+), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for volatility or downward correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently fails to capture late-cycle corrections; adjust horizon by reducing final 5–7 days’ forecast slope if sentiment turns negative.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5 days, model is likely overconfident; apply early correction rule: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
